evidence.claim: Julesburg served the Pony Express in 1860–1861; Fort Sedgwick followed in 1864 to guard the trail and telegraph.
evidence.quote: Julesburg was on the Pony Express (1860–1861) route from Missouri to California.

evidence.claim: After the U.S. Army’s Sand Creek Massacre of Cheyenne and Arapaho people, Cheyenne, Arapaho and Lakota warriors attacked Julesburg in January 1865 and returned to burn the settlement in February.
evidence.quote: The U.S. Army's Sand Creek Massacre of Cheyenne and Arapaho on November 29, 1864, caused a large number of Indians on the Kansas and Colorado Great Plains to intensify hostilities against the U.S. Army and white settlers.

evidence.claim: In 1867, Julesburg became a Union Pacific construction town, housing workers as the railroad advanced west.

evidence.claim: The brick depot at Julesburg combined passengers, freight and express shipments under one roof. Union Pacific built this single-story station in 1930 to a standard combination-depot design.
evidence.quote: It is a brick, one-story building built as a standard Union Pacific Railroad "combination-type" depot, i.e. handling passengers as well as freight and express shipments.

evidence.claim: A tornado badly damaged it in June 1947, but the building was repaired. In 1974 it moved a short distance and became a museum.
evidence.quote: The depot was hit by a tornado on June 6, 1947, that badly damaged the building;  it was repaired.  In 1974 it was moved a short distance and turned into a museum.

evidence.claim: Its National Register recognition in 2004 acknowledged both its transportation role and the design, materials and workmanship preserved through that move.
evidence.quote: It was listed on the National Register in 2004.  It was deemed significant for its role in transportation and the economic growth of Julesburg, and architecturally for its design, materials, and workmanship which are preserved despite the building having been moved a short distance.

evidence.claim: Union Pacific built this single-story station in 1930
evidence.quote: The Union Pacific Railroad Julesburg Depot, at 210 W. First St. in Julesburg, Colorado, and also known as the Depot Museum, was built in 1930.

evidence.claim: Fort Sedgwick has markers in place of buildings. The military post operated from 1864 to 1871; after its abandonment, the buildings were dismantled.
evidence.quote: The post was abandoned in May 1871 and the buildings were dismantled.

Sources differ in tribal terminology: Julesburg and battle articles name Cheyenne, Arapaho and Lakota; Fort Sedgwick says Cheyenne and Sioux. The specific names in the battle article are used; casualty counts are omitted because accounts conflict. No tribal-authored cache source is available.
Current grave-count and firewood claims have cache support only as reports by named military officers. They are omitted as editorial choices, not evidence failures.
